Hi all — quick note from infra/perf: 

Test account & key:
- I’ve created a temporary test project and API key: FW-TEST-2026-07 (valid until 2026-07-16).
- Test endpoint: https://api-test.redwood.ai/v1/finwise

IP allowlist (suggested CIDR ranges for FinWise firewall):
- 34.82.120.0/24
- 34.82.121.0/24
- 52.23.45.0/24

Load test guidance (summary):
- For non-streaming (embeddings): k6 is fine — use the attached k6 script as a starting point. Ramp: 5m warm-up, then 10m linear ramp to target RPS, hold 30m, then cool-down 5m.
- For streaming (chat/token streaming): Locust with a WebSocket client or a small Python harness is recommended to simulate streaming token flows. k6 doesn’t model token-by-token streaming well.
- Warm-up / cache priming: run ~2–3 minutes of representative requests per route before ramp to populate KV cache and embeddings cache.
- KV/cache note: if you want to validate cold-start behavior run a separate short test after a 1h idle period.

Recommendation for ramp stages (chat streaming):
1) 2m steady baseline at 10% load
2) 8m linear ramp to 60%
3) 10m linear ramp to 100% (peak)
4) 30m hold at peak to observe sustained behavior
5) 10m cool-down

Monitoring notes for Redwood team: we’ll surface p50/p95/p99 latencies, token emission rates (streaming), error rates by route, and model fallback events. Please ensure you have logging from the client to correlate streams with server traces.

Attachments included: test-account-instructions.txt, locustfile_streaming.py (sample).

—Aditya
